task: Review BoundedFileReader for oversized/symlink/nonregular/mutation cases and limit enforcement without unbounded allocation.

tests.result: Inspected descriptor opening and final-component rejection: O_NOFOLLOW rejects symlinks; O_NONBLOCK prevents FIFO open from waiting; fstat checks the opened regular-file descriptor before reserveCapacity/read; descriptor is closed by defer.

Initial st_size above maximumBytes fails before allocation. Limits reject negatives and Int.max, so maximumBytes + 1 cannot overflow. Reads request at most min(65536, maximumBytes + 1 - contents.count); contents above the limit throws immediately. Growing files therefore cannot yield unbounded logical bytes. Data capacity/allocator overhead was not measured.

Confirmed production limits: document import 8 MiB; reference-photo import 32 MiB. ProjectDocumentIO supplies NSFileCoordinator around the read; ReferencePhoto reads a provider-owned temporary file during transfer callback.

Read all 13 BoundedFileReaderTests methods covering metadata checks, nonexistent metadata, preflight/open replacement, actual task cancellation, empty/exact-limit reads, oversized inputs, symlinks/directories/FIFOs, replacement after open, growth after fstat, callback cancellation, invalid limits and missing/nonfile URLs. No test methods executed.
No compiler probe, native XCTest, full suite, Apple runtime, or allocator measurement performed. Review was read-only; only this temporary report was written.

outcome: No concrete material defect found within the bounded-reader review. Open-descriptor identity and byte-limit logic address the assigned pathname/growth cases. The reader does not independently guarantee a snapshot against uncoordinated in-place writes, consistent with its explicit caller-coordination responsibility; no production workflow failure established.
